key_insight: An LLM-based workflow assesses psychotherapy fidelity and generates supervisory feedback, with evidence-first reasoning improving fidelity estimates.
clinical_relevance: The approach could expand access to therapy supervision and support clinician learning, though improved patient outcomes were not established.
method: Compare three open-weight LLMs across task decompositions and reasoning strategies.
Generate fidelity assessments and actionable supervisory feedback.
evidence_signal: On an independent RCT dataset, the framework distinguished CBT from non-CBT sessions across core therapeutic skills; mental health experts also judged generated feedback actionable.
watch_item: The abstract does not report sample sizes or quantitative performance, limiting assessment of reliability for routine supervision.
paper_title: Scaling Therapy Supervision: Assessing Psychotherapy Fidelity Using Large Language Models
